title: Speaking up behaviours of professional working in clinical institutions regarding (sexualized) violence against patients
summary:
In clinical institutions, conscious or unconscious professional misconduct, (sexual) assaults and (sexual) violence by healthcare professionals can lead to negative situations for patients. The aim of clinical institutions must be to become a place of protection for the patients entrusted to them. The extent to which professional misconduct is addressed or reported by colleagues (speaking up) plays one role here. This study therefore investigates 1) how often employees in clinical institutions have noticed different types of professional misconduct by colleagues; 2) how often they have spoken up about such behaviour or remained silent about it; 3) what their reasons were for not speaking up about such behaviour; 4) how they generally assess communication regarding patient safety in their working environment and 5) how likely they think it is that they will speak up about misconduct in such situations in the future. To this end, employees from various professional groups who work in clinical institutions are surveyed using an online questionnaire. 
We assume that low speaking up behaviour in the past and a poor communication climate are associated with a lower probability of speaking up about misconduct in the future. We also assume that misconduct of people higher up in the hierarchy would be less likely spoken up about.
In addition, the study aims to gain knowledge about the key motives for professionals not to speak up about concerns regarding patient safety.
conditions: Professional misconduct, (sexual) assaults and (sexual) violence against patients
